children: Jindal Worldwide shares hit the 20 per cent upper circuit limit on Thursday, snapping the previous session's nearly 5 per cent fall, after its electric vehicle arm announced plans to expand its retail network to around 100 showrooms across the country by the end of FY28.
The stock hit a high of Rs 48.22 per share on the NSE, gaining 20 per cent, the highest permissible trading limit for the stock during the session.

The sharp rise came after Jindal Mobilitric Private Limited, the electric vehicle arm and subsidiary of Jindal Worldwide Ltd, announced plans to scale its retail network to approximately 100 showrooms across India by the end of FY28.
The expansion is part of the company's strategy to strengthen last-mile customer experience and accelerate EV adoption nationwide.

The company had made the filing with the stock exchanges after market hours on August 31. Subsequently, the stock rose 10 per cent in the next session on Tuesday, before falling 4.5 per cent on Wednesday.
On Thursday, the stock again jumped 20 per cent amid renewed interest.
As part of the phased expansion, the company plans to open around 40 showrooms by the end of FY27, with the remaining outlets to be commissioned progressively through FY28.
The rollout is aimed at ensuring consistent customer experience, after-sales support and disciplined capital allocation as the network expands, the company said.

"Reaching 100 showrooms by FY28 is an ambitious goal, but one we are fully committed to and excited about. We see the next two years as a defining growth phase for the Company, and we are confident of delivering strong, sustained results for our shareholders as we build one of India's most trusted electric mobility brands," said Amit Agarwal, Director, Jindal Mobilitric Private Limited.
The company has already commenced commercial operations, with its manufacturing facility in Ahmedabad fully operational.

Jindal Mobilitric has opened its first two showrooms in Srinagar and Jaipur, marking the beginning of its pan-India retail expansion. Early customer footfalls and conversions at these showrooms have been encouraging, it said.
The company has also appointed 52 dealers across the country, building a distribution network to support the planned showroom expansion and market penetration across urban and semi-urban areas.
